NDT training in the Southeast: how it works

Short answer: Southeast candidates and employers train with Atlantis NDT in three steps: self-paced theory online, supported by an ASNT Level III who answers technical questions; rehearsal in the Practical NDT simulator in a browser; and hands-on training with the practical examination at the employer's plant, hangar or yard. The employer certifies the technician afterward, under a written practice based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A.

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in the Southeast, and its offices are in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India. That matters less than it sounds, because the theory is online and the hands-on part happens at the employer. You can enroll in any month, and access to the course opens as soon as you do. The ASNT NDT Level III behind the courses holds UT, RT, MT, PT and VT and has spent more than 11 years in field inspection.

What sets the Southeast apart is how many qualification regimes share it. A technician in the Carolinas or Georgia can work aerospace manufacturing, nuclear plants and ship repair without moving, and employers value people who understand more than one rulebook. This guide explains how training and certification work for an individual entering or progressing in NDT, and for an employer qualifying a team.

Where NDT technicians work across the Southeast

Aerospace in the Lowcountry and coastal Georgia. Boeing assembles 787 Dreamliners in North Charleston and broke ground on a site expansion there in November 2025. Gulfstream builds and services business jets in Savannah. Both draw a supplier base of machining, composites and metal finishing shops that perform penetrant, eddy current and ultrasonic examination to customer requirements. See NDT training in North Charleston and NDT training in Savannah.

Atlanta's aircraft and maintenance base. Lockheed Martin builds the C-130J in Marietta, and Delta TechOps maintains engines and airframes at Hartsfield-Jackson. Maintenance work leans on eddy current, penetrant and ultrasonic inspection under OEM manuals and FAA repair station rules. See NDT training in Atlanta.

Nuclear: the Savannah River Site, Vogtle and the Carolinas fleet. The Department of Energy's Savannah River Site near Aiken runs construction, operations and cleanup work under nuclear quality programs. Across the river in Georgia, Plant Vogtle added two new units, which entered commercial service in 2023 and 2024. Duke Energy runs several nuclear stations in the Carolinas, and TVA operates Sequoyah and Watts Bar in Tennessee. Outages at these plants bring in UT, PT, VT and eddy current crews. See NDT training in Aiken, NDT training in Charlotte and NDT training in Chattanooga.

Oak Ridge and East Tennessee. The Y-12 National Security Complex and Oak Ridge National Laboratory add federal nuclear and research work, each with its own quality requirements. See NDT training in Oak Ridge and NDT training in Knoxville.

Ship repair and naval aviation in Jacksonville. Naval Station Mayport hosts surface ships whose maintenance supports a local ship repair industry, and Fleet Readiness Center Southeast at Naval Air Station Jacksonville overhauls military aircraft. JAXPORT's terminals add port, crane and tank work. See NDT training in Jacksonville.

Nashville and Middle Tennessee. Vehicle assembly at Nissan's Smyrna plant, a broad base of metal fabrication, structural steel for a growing city and industrial equipment makers make Nashville a weld-inspection market: VT, MT and UT under AWS D1.1. See NDT training in Nashville.

Which NDT methods and levels Southeast employers ask for

The mix of regimes means the same method can be judged against very different documents depending on who you work for. The table maps each sector to the methods it requests and the rules that decide acceptance.

SectorMethods requestedRules that decide acceptance
Aircraft and engine manufactureFluorescent PT, UT, ET, MT, RTPrime and customer specifications, ASTM E1417 and E1444 practices, Nadcap AC7114 audits
Aircraft maintenance and overhaulET, PT, UT, VTOEM NDT manuals and FAA Part 145 repair station requirements; military maintenance manuals at naval depots
Commercial nuclear plantsUT, PT, VT, MT, ETASME Section XI in service and Section III for new components, under the utility's nuclear quality program
Federal nuclear sitesVT, PT, UT, RTContract specifications citing ASME and AWS codes, under the site's quality assurance program
Ship repair and naval workVT, MT, UT, PTNAVSEA requirements and MIL-STD-2035 for naval ships; class society rules for commercial vessels
Structural steel and vehicle plantsVT, MT, UTAWS D1.1 and customer specifications
Fossil and gas-fired generationUT, MT, PT, VTASME Section I and ASME B31.1

For a newcomer, the surface methods come early: VT and PT suit aerospace and nuclear employers, while VT and MT suit fabricators and ship repair. UT is the method that crosses all three regimes, so it is worth adding as soon as your employer can give you experience in it. Start at NDT Level 1 training, progress through NDT Level 2 training, and see ultrasonic testing training and eddy current testing training for the methods aircraft maintenance relies on.

How NDT certification works across state lines in the Southeast

The Southeast's state lines run through its job markets: Aiken and Augusta face each other across the Savannah River, and Chattanooga sits on the Georgia border. SNT-TC-1A ignores those lines. The certificate comes from the employer, under its written practice, and it stops when you leave; your next employer recertifies you under its own. No course certifies a technician, ours included.

What travels is your evidence. Course records that show hours and topics, an experience log signed by your supervisors and up-to-date vision results let a new employer's Level III accept your history and move straight to examinations. Our SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker shows what each level requires, and the state pages for South Carolina, Georgia and Tennessee add local detail.

Each regime adds its own layer, and the employer is responsible for it. Aerospace primes flow NDT requirements down to suppliers, Nadcap AC7114 audits check compliance, and the employer's written practice is built on SNT-TC-1A and aligned with that flow-down. Commercial nuclear work adds ASME Section XI and performance demonstration for ultrasonic examination. Federal nuclear sites add their own quality assurance requirements. Naval ship and aircraft work adds NAVSEA and naval aviation requirements. A technician who knows where SNT-TC-1A ends and the overlay begins is the person Southeast employers want for cross-regime work.

If you would rather hold a credential that follows you, ASNT NDT Level II and ASNT NDT Level III are examined and issued by ASNT, and you keep them when you change jobs, subject to each employer's acceptance. Atlantis prepares candidates for those examinations, and the ASNT certification guide sets out the details.

Radiography and federal sites in the Southeast

In legal terms, RT training gives you method knowledge and nothing more: it does not entitle you to handle a source. The radioactive materials license is held by the employer, and a radiographer must also complete radiation safety training and a radiographer certification examination before working without direct supervision.

Two Southeast situations deserve a closer look. The first is federal property. Work at a Department of Energy site such as Savannah River also has to satisfy the site's own radiological controls, and work in areas of exclusive federal jurisdiction, which can include parts of military installations, falls to the NRC rather than the state. The second is cross-border work: a crew based in one state that takes jobs across the Savannah River or into Tennessee needs its license holder to file for reciprocity before the job starts.

For a trainee, the route is the same everywhere. Find an employer that already holds a license and runs radiation safety training, then take radiographic testing training for the method itself.

Choosing an NDT training provider in the Southeast

Southeast candidates choose among technical college programs, private NDT schools, training inside a large employer, and self-paced online theory combined with a practical at the employer. Each has a fair case. College programs give structured lab time to people with no industry experience. Schools offer concentrated method courses. Large aerospace and nuclear employers often train new hires internally to their own programs. Online theory fits people who already have an employer, or are about to, and need the hours without leaving work.

Questions that separate one option from another:

  • Will the target employer's Level III accept the hours? Aerospace and nuclear employers in particular may have specific rules, so ask before enrolling.
  • Does the course cover the method's SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge at the level you need?
  • Who is available to answer questions, and which methods do they hold at Level III?
  • How is hands-on practice arranged, and who examines the practical?
  • Does the completion record list hours and topics in a form an auditor will accept?

Our route is described on the NDT training courses and NDT training in the USA pages, and the published US course fees are on this page.

Training a crew across several Southeast sites

Employers in the region often split crews between a manufacturing plant and outage or field work, sometimes in different states. Atlantis brings the training to the employer: technicians complete theory online, then hands-on training and practical examinations take place at the company's facility on its own equipment and parts, under ASNT Level III oversight.

For a company that serves aerospace and nuclear customers at the same time, the written practice carries most of the weight. One document built on SNT-TC-1A, with sections that address each customer's flow-down, keeps certifications consistent and audit trails clean across sites. We can write or revise it through NDT written practice development and set up examinations and records through SNT-TC-1A training program setup. Train ahead of the spring and fall outage seasons so the outages supply supervised hours. Send the methods, levels, sites and customers, and we reply within one business day.

Get ready for the practical with simulation and practice tests

Hands-on access is scarce for many Southeast trainees, especially in aerospace plants where production parts cannot be tied up for practice. The Practical NDT simulator, which works in a browser, on a PC or in VR, lets you repeat the steps of an examination, from setup and calibration to recording, as often as you need. It is preparation only: it does not count toward experience hours, and the employer's practical examination still decides.

The free NDT practice tests give you Level II questions in UT, PAUT, TOFD, ET, RT, MT, PT and VT with explanations. Use them to check your understanding when you finish a theory module.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in the Southeast

Answers that apply in every region are in the NDT training FAQ.

How long does NDT training take in the Southeast?

Self-paced theory for one method usually takes a few weeks of steady study, with VT, MT and PT the shortest and UT and RT the longest. The employer's written practice sets the final hours, and certification also needs supervised experience on the job.

Can I study NDT online from Atlanta, Charleston or Jacksonville?

Yes, for the theory, with Level III support online. Hands-on training and the practical examination happen in person at your employer's facility. See online NDT training.

Is there an Atlantis NDT training location near me in the Southeast?

No. Atlantis has no walk-in site in any Southeast state. Employers receive training at their own facility, and individuals study online and complete the practical at the employer they work for or are joining.

Which method is a good starting point for aerospace or nuclear work?

PT and VT, because both regimes use them constantly and they are quick to learn. Add UT next, since it is used in manufacture, maintenance and outages alike. Aircraft maintenance roles also value eddy current.

Does my NDT certification transfer if I move from Georgia to the Carolinas?

The certificate itself does not, because it belongs to the employer that issued it. Your training and experience records do transfer, and a new employer typically re-examines you and recertifies you under its own written practice. ASNT central certification is the portable alternative.

Can I prepare for ASNT NDT Level III in the Southeast?

Yes, online. Our self-paced ASNT Level III training prepares experienced Level IIs for ASNT's Basic and method examinations. ASNT checks your experience, runs the examinations and issues the certificate.

Is AWS CWI exam prep available for the Southeast?

Yes. The six-day AWS CWI exam prep course is available as a corporate course at your facility, online, or one-to-one, online or in person. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification. AWS CWI training in North Charleston and Memphis have local detail.
